reason: The S3 access points section of What is Amazon S3 states each access point has its own policy, Block Public Access per access point, and that any access point can be configured to accept requests only from a VPC.

Under 'Storage classes for rarely accessed objects' the three Glacier classes are designed for low-cost long-term storage and require minimum storage durations and retrieval fees, most effective for rarely accessed data.

The Provisioned capacity section states all three parts: capacity for Expedited retrievals from Flexible Retrieval, possible non-acceptance without it during high demand, and that the requester, not the bucket owner, should buy the units.

The Restoring large datasets section names the per-account retrieval-requests quota for the three storage classes, the 1,000 TPS rate, throttling with ThrottlingException, Batch Operations, and increased restoration limits through AWS Support.

The lifecycle considerations page states the temporary copy, the duration set in the request, deletion of the copy, the unchanged storage class, the double charge (archive rate plus S3 Standard rate) and one restore request at a time per object.

The table row for Flexible Retrieval or Intelligent-Tiering Archive Access gives 1–5 minutes, Minutes–5 hours with Batch Operations, 3–5 hours and 5–12 hours; the Expedited bullet limits 1–5 minutes to objects under 250 megabytes.

The authorization page states S3 evaluates all relevant user and resource policies, the bucket-context rules for bucket and object requests with explicit deny, and that the parent account is the context authority in the user context.
The S3 pricing page says live replication (CRR, SRR) replicates newly uploaded objects as written, while S3 Batch Replication replicates existing objects as fully managed Batch Operations jobs.

The Block Public Access page states account settings apply to all buckets and access points the account owns and to all Regions with eventual propagation, recommends all four settings for the account, and recommends BlockPublicPolicy at account level with the stated effect.

The page states four independent settings usable in any combination at access point, bucket or account level and the most restrictive combination rule; the settings table names IgnorePublicAcls, RestrictPublicBuckets, BlockPublicPolicy and refers to BlockPublicAcls as a setting.
The Bucket Keys page states a bucket-level key for SSE-KMS can reduce AWS KMS request costs by up to 99 percent by decreasing request traffic from S3 to KMS.

What is Amazon S3 states bucket policies are limited to 20 KB, and the access control page states both bucket policies and identity-based policies have a 20 KB limit that complex requirements might exceed.

The Bynder case study states its access patterns frequently change, making traditional storage less cost effective, and quotes its engineering manager saying Intelligent-Tiering reviews access patterns automatically.

The bucket quotas page gives a default of 10,000 general purpose buckets per account, the 2015 history row gives the earlier default of 100, and the 2024-11-14 What's New item (checked in changes s3.jsonl line 161) says any customer can request an increase up to 1 million buckets.

The document history row dated August 20, 2024 announces conditional writes for PutObject and CompleteMultipartUpload, and the conditional writes page says If-None-Match makes the operation fail when an identical key name exists, preventing overwrites.
The storage classes page says Flexible Retrieval is for archives where portions might need retrieval in minutes and its data is archived and not available for real-time access.
The storage classes page says Glacier Instant Retrieval is for rarely accessed long-term data that needs milliseconds retrieval and is available for real-time access.
The security best practices page says with client-side encryption you encrypt client-side, upload the encrypted data, and manage the encryption process, keys and related tools.
The bucket policy examples page shows a policy that grants a CloudFront OAI permission to get all objects so users access them through CloudFront but not directly through S3.

The CORS page gives the definition and Scenario 1: JavaScript on the website endpoint making authenticated GET and PUT requests to the API endpoint, which a browser would block unless the bucket's CORS configuration enables them.

The security best practices page states SSE-S3 is the default encryption configuration for every bucket and a different type can be set in PUT requests or in the destination bucket's default encryption.
The Storage classes section of What is Amazon S3 states the lowest latency class claim with access speeds up to 10x faster and request costs 80 percent lower than S3 Standard.
The FAQ answer states the pending and latency metrics cannot track Batch Replication progress and that the operations failed metric can monitor objects that fail to replicate.
The FAQ answer states Deep Archive is a separate line item on the monthly bill but is included under S3 usage in AWS Cost Management detailed monthly spend reports.
The FAQ says 'From just $0.00099 per GB-month', about $1 per TB-month, which supports a starting (lowest) price.
The FAQ says each S3 directory bucket can support up to 2 million TPS, independent of the number of directories in the bucket.
The FAQ says S3 is designed to provide 99.999999999% (11 nines) data durability.
The FAQ says Expedited and Standard have a per-GB retrieval fee and per-request fee, and Bulk retrievals from Flexible Retrieval are free.
The FAQ gives 1-5 minutes for Expedited except objects of 250MB+, 3-5 hours for Standard with a start in minutes through Batch Operations, and 5-12 hours for free Bulk retrievals.
The FAQ says AWS offers eligible customers free data transfer out to the internet when they move all their data off AWS, following the described process.
The FAQ says objects in the Frequent, Infrequent and Archive Instant Access tiers can be lifecycled to One Zone-IA, Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Glacier Deep Archive.
The FAQ says with Versioning and MFA Delete, permanently deleting a version requires account credentials plus a valid six-digit code and serial number from a device you possess.
The FAQ says that if all or part of an Availability Zone is lost or damaged, data in a One Zone storage class may be lost.
The FAQ says S3 One Zone-IA offers a 99% available SLA and is designed for eleven 9's of durability within the Availability Zone.
The FAQ says S3 Replication supports all encryption types S3 offers and lists SSE-S3, SSE-KMS and SSE-C for server-side encryption; the claim's 'among' keeps the list non-exhaustive.

The FAQ says Transfer Acceleration speeds long-distance transfers of larger objects to a single bucket, while Multi-Region Access Points do similar transfers across many buckets in multiple Regions over the AWS global network.
The FAQ says Tape Gateway archives new virtual tapes directly to Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive and moves tape backups to AWS without changes to existing backup workflows.
The Glacier quotas table row gives provisioned capacity units 'Each supported Region: 2', not adjustable, as the maximum available to purchase per account.

The Intelligent-Tiering overview gives the monitoring charge, the moves after 30 consecutive days and 90 days without performance impact, and that objects under 128 KB are not monitored and stay in Frequent Access.

The overview gives minimums of 90 and 180 consecutive days, configurable days, a 730-day maximum stated for both the Archive Access and Deep Archive Access tiers, and the RestoreObject requirement before reading.
